definitions.gloss: to wail; to cry loudly; to sob uncontrollably
definitions.explanation: To cry loudly and openly, with audible sobbing. Stronger than simply crying (泣く). Often used in dramatic or emotional contexts.

examples.japanese: {感動|かんどう}して{号泣|ごうきゅう}した。
examples.english: I was so moved that I cried my eyes out.

examples.japanese: {映画|えいが}のラストシーンで{観客|かんきゃく}が{号泣|ごうきゅう}していた。
examples.english: The audience was sobbing during the last scene of the movie.

examples.japanese: {卒業式|そつぎょうしき}で{友達|ともだち}との{別|わか}れが{辛|つら}くて、{人前|ひとまえ}で{号泣|ごうきゅう}してしまった。
examples.english: At the graduation ceremony, parting with my friends was so painful that I ended up wailing in front of everyone.

notes:
USAGE:
Originally a strong literary word meaning to cry with loud, audible sobs. In modern casual usage, especially online and among younger speakers, {号泣|ごうきゅう} is often used more loosely to mean "crying a lot" or even "tearing up," somewhat diluting its original intensity.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {感動|かんどう}して{号泣|ごうきゅう}する (to cry from being moved)
- {人前|ひとまえ}で{号泣|ごうきゅう}する (to cry in public)
- {号泣|ごうきゅう}する{映画|えいが} (a movie that makes you cry)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {泣|な}く: The basic word for crying — neutral in intensity.
- {涙|なみだ}を{流|なが}す: To shed tears — more literary, can be quiet.
- {嗚咽|おえつ}する: To sob, to choke up — emphasizes the physical act of sobbing with a constricted voice.
